item.title: Issue #2997 created
item.description:
JNodes: fewer jvalue() calls?

I wonder what we could do to get rid of the cumbersome ! jvalue() invocations. The current JMESPath tests have 290 of them alone, most of which cannot be avoided. In the JSONPath tests, I could only circumvent them by adding jtree(...) wrappers in the test assertions.

We could let the attribute axis mean “value of the child JNode”:

$in/foo ! { "bar": @bar, "baz": @baz }    (: bar ! jvalue(), baz ! jvalue() :)
array { @* }                              (: array { * ! jvalue() } :)
sort($in/numbers/@*)                      (: values, sorted :)
$in/foo/*[exists(@key)]                   (: key exists and is not null :)
$in/foo/*[deep-equal(@key, [ 0 ])]

Another syntax extension could be a new “value” axis: value::*.

Someone suggested /?, but I assume it would result in ambiguities ($in/foo ! jvalue() → $in/foo/?)

A more radical approach would be to ignore JNode/XNode boundaries. The following query…

let $nodes := { 'nodes': [ <xml><w/></xml> ] }/nodes
return jvalue($nodes/1)//w

…could then be simplified to:

{ 'nodes': [ <xml><w/></xml> ] }/nodes/1//w

I haven’t reflected on the implications; suggestions are welcome.
